why: Point updates (move a dividend) mixed with prefix-sum queries (all dividends paid by day d) over a fixed day range: a Fenwick tree indexed by day gives both in O(log D).
hints: A price query subtracts every dividend paid on or before the day. That is a prefix sum over days. What makes a plain prefix array fail?
Updates change the array between queries. Keep a Fenwick tree indexed by day where position day holds the total dividend paid that day.
UPDATE: add -old_amount at old_day, then +new_amount at new_day. PRICE d: stockPrice - prefix(d). O(log 10^6) each.
pitfalls: Remember each dividend's current (amount, day) so an update can remove the old one.
Several dividends may share a day; the tree stores their sum.
